title: Thursday's page
how: Wednesday's four open looks, taken again in the game at full size. Tap any picture or face to open it full-screen at its full resolution: pinch to zoom, swipe to the next, Close to come back. One tap each; a note is optional. Your picks save on the page.
foot: Anything you do not pick carries onto the next page. Your three picks from this morning are in (the voice: this week's items first, with your condition; both thinking sounds: the loudness mouth).

sections.name: The street by day, with its 1990 clutter: does anything jar?
sections.detail: Taken today in the game at 2560 by 1440, through its own light and exposure (Wednesday's were half that). In it: the telephone kiosk, pillar box, galvanised dustbins, bollards, litter bins, the telegraph pole and its wires, the grit bin; each passed my check and a blind reviewer's, which under your rule is their approval. The third view is cropped at the bottom, where that camera stands just behind a builder's skip. Today's reviewer passed it, with notes: the near car's windscreen is opaque grey and its plate blank; the other figures' hair shows a flat silver patch on the crown and the woman in the doorway stands stiffly, arms straight down (they are the three placeholders of 23 September, replaced by MetaHuman townspeople for the friends' build); Sheila's hair reads grey in the second view and near-black in the first. Wednesday's: the kiosk's glass shows no tint or reflection; two telegraph wires seem to end at the chimneys from the far end.

sections.name: The street at night under its sodium lamps: does it read as night?
sections.detail: The same three views at ten at night, taken today at 2560 by 1440 through the game's own light and exposure. Low-pressure sodium, one orange colour, pools of light under each lamp and the gaps between left dark, the wet road carrying their reflections (from the research on 1990 street light). Today's reviewer passed it, with notes: in the third view the lamps' light ends in hard arcs across the upper floor; the pillar box stays bright red. Wednesday's: the left terrace's brick is lit fairly evenly up to the eaves, nearer floodlighting than pools; colours survive the sodium light, where under real sodium they would go orange and black; the cream tiles under the right-hand shop are the brightest patch; the lit upstairs windows read cool rather than warm.

sections.name: Their mouths as they answer: roughly in time with the words?
sections.detail: Filmed in the game today from 60 cm while each answered, the mouth following the loudness of the voice you hear (the way your picks this morning chose for the thinking sounds too). The words are the test stand-in's, not a real reply. The film catches about seven frames a second and plays at ten, each frame placed by how much of the sentence had been heard when it was taken, so it moves coarsely; the game is smooth. In play the second sentence comes about 1.5 s after the first, while the voice makes it; here the pause is under a second. Darren still wears his earlier head in the game; S6, which you approved, goes in next. The first reviewer failed an earlier cut of these films: the mouth trailed the sound by a third of a second, because the film counted from the moment the sound was set playing, not heard; fixed, and the film's motion blur turned off (at seven frames a second a turn of the head smeared). A fresh reviewer passed the fixed films: the mouth follows the sound to within about a frame. Its notes: each sentence's mouth opens a frame late; in the pause the picture holds for half a second, then jumps; inside Sheila's mouth reads grey-green in a few frames, and a pale speckled line runs along her upper eyelid crease; the tops of the heads are cut off. Earlier notes: every open mouth is roughly the same oval; the teeth have ragged, yellowish edges.

sections.name: Ron's work boots and Sheila's handbag: do they stay?
sections.detail: The clothing session's first pieces, fitted in the game and taken today at full size in the street's own light: Ron's black work boots (in place of Epic's, lifting him 2 cm onto their soles) and Sheila's chestnut handbag in her right hand. Clothes on people are yours to approve. The green post at the edge of the boots is a litter bin on the pavement. Today's reviewer passed it, with notes: the boots' close view is dark, in the shop front's shade, so zoom in; each toe shows a small gap between the upper and the sole; the handbag's handles pass through her fingers rather than lying in their curl; the bag is plain brown with no texture and hangs a little tilted; a piece of litter overlaps her shoes. Earlier reviewers': the boots' collar a little ragged, the sole even with no heel step, the laces flat; the bag a little boxy, no metal loops at the handles. Her spectacles are held back to be refitted to her approved head.
